learner_operation: Use elementary row elimination to decide which residual rows vanish, then count pivots in REF and select that integer. Matrix dimensions alone give a bound, not the answer.

fixed_features.feature: One five-option numeric radio field asking for number of pivot columns
fixed_features.justification: All 17 assessed source questions use selection/radio, five integer choices. The task is a count rather than column identities.

fixed_features.feature: Sparse 3–5 row, 5–6 column matrices in normal sampling and one or two row replacements
fixed_features.justification: Matches the assessed moderate source workload; the canonical 3x4 example has no captured radio control and is not a replay template.

fixed_features.feature: No row-swap branch or symbolic parameters
fixed_features.justification: The supplied target KP cases use one/two row replacements; extending to extra cases is unnecessary for this review.

answer_roles.role: Survival of a residual row after elimination
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Zero versus nonzero residual at the same dimensions and with the same elimination roles
answer_roles.observed: Controlled 3x5 pair changes one entry and rank 2 -> 3. All 17 templates show multiple ranks in independent control. Exact batch fixes corank one in all five records.

answer_roles.eligible_variation: Vary pivot count within comparable elimination workload and shift pivot locations; derive answer and explanation from actual matrix
answer_roles.observed: Control sample covers ranks 2–5 and shifted pivot columns. No justified rule requires rows-minus-one.

answer_roles.role: Correct numeric choice and its presentation position
answer_roles.eligible_variation: Derive numeric choice from rank; labels and shuffled order must not identify it
answer_roles.observed: All 155 tested native grader submissions behave correctly. UI independently orders choices by field and item IDs; numeric rows-minus-one bypass is unaffected by this ordering.

coverage.case: All captured assessed source templates and banks
coverage.result: 17 replayed, exact input/intermediate/final matrices and full banks/keys match; no excluded assessed cases.

coverage.case: Residual survival variation in independently chosen normal seeds
coverage.result: 204/204 survive shared filtering, no generation exceptions, every template has at least two observed ranks.
All five survive delivery and all have rank equal to rows minus one: rows [4,4,3,3,5], answers [3,3,2,2,4].

All are moderate. Any positive moderate weight selects uniformly among eligible moderate IDs; when only proposed items remain fresh, every draw retains shortcut (64/64). Explicit combined captured-bank scenario has counterexamples.

counterfactuals.change: For q-130957, seed 74109 with explicit parameters, change final residual entry (row 3, column 5) from 0 to 1, holding all other entries, name and operations fixed. Only one input cell changes.
counterfactuals.expected: Rank and accepted numeric choice change 2 -> 3; prompt shows new entry and solution retains third pivot. Old choice becomes wrong.
counterfactuals.observed: Exact matrix/solution check passes; both rendered screenshots show the change; native grader accepts 2 only before and 3 only after, rejecting each of the other four choices.
counterfactuals.justification: Dependence after elimination is the target operation; source f1ae8763-ab2d-5aee-9b53-3f6da8520aee loses a row, whereas 02683bf4-c015-5b9c-845b-c5f836ec3faf retains a later pivot.

counterfactuals.change: Rename A to D, and separately rescale the first nonzero REF row by 2 with corresponding input reconstruction; hold residual survival fixed.
counterfactuals.expected: Rank and accepted numeric answer remain 3; labels/row values change consistently.
counterfactuals.observed: Both variants have exact rank 3, correct solution conclusion, no math errors, and native grader accepts only 3. Rendered name/scale variants pass the actual UI renderer.
counterfactuals.justification: Matrix labels are incidental and nonzero row scaling preserves row equivalence; elementary row operations are the source prerequisite.

stages_examined: learner history exclusions and difficulty-first weighted selection rules
delivery.result: Captured basis 5362: controls 204 -> 204, batch 5 -> 5. Normalization rewrites identities but preserves prompts, solutions, bank values and answers. Batch-only fresh pool remains 100% solvable by row count minus one under all within-pool orderings/exclusions. Combined bank is not uniformly vulnerable.

limitations: No finite sample proves absence of all shortcuts.

Actual active learner policy/history and new publication entity IDs are not captured. Selection scenarios explicitly use hypothetical fresh IDs and the inspected production rule; no database writes occur.
Canonical example lacks answer-field evidence and is not exposed as a source-replay template; its matrices and rank are independently confirmed, without inventing an answer control.

The demonstrated finding is finite-batch selection, not universal sampler failure. All 22 captured inventory questions were tested for that predicate; no affected stored pool-wide defect demonstrated.
